section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the three levels of "daughter," "sister," and "mother" in the Midrash, corresponding to the three pilgrimage festivals of Pesach, Shavuos, and Sukkos, and how the level of "daughter" relates to the future redemption through self-nullification.
section.t: And this can be understood based on what is stated in the Midrash:
A parable of a king, etc. He did not cease cherishing her
until He called her "My daughter," etc. He did not cease cherishing her until He called her "My sister," etc. He did not cease cherishing her until He called her "My mother."
And it is explained in the discourses,
that these three matters
(daughter, sister, mother)
correspond to the three pilgrimage festivals.
For at the Exodus from Egypt
(Pesach),
when Israel were in a state of nakedness and bereft of mitzvos,
and the redemption was through a revelation from Above,
the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself upon them in His very glory and redeemed them,
they were called by the name "My daughter,"
for a daughter is a level of receiver,
who has nothing of her own and is only a receiver of that which is given to her from Above.
And at the Giving of the Torah
(Shavuos),
they are called by the name "My sister,"
for through the Torah they become brothers and companions to the Holy One, blessed be He.
And in general terms,
through the Torah, Israel become one with the Holy One, blessed be He,
[as is known in the explanation of the statement,
"Israel, the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one,"
for through Israel being one with the Torah, they thereby become one with the Holy One, blessed be He].
And through Teshuvah
(which is above Torah),
they are called by the name "My mother,"
for they, as it were, bestow influence upon the Holy One, blessed be He.
As it is stated,
"Go out and see, O daughters of Zion, King Shlomo with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding," and it is taught in the Mishnah
that "the day of his wedding" is Yom Kippur,
for through the Teshuvah of Yom Kippur
(for on Yom Kippur is the perfection of Teshuvah),
the Congregation of Israel crowns the Holy One, blessed be He, with a crown.
And since the revelation of Teshuvah and atonement of Yom Kippur is [manifested] in the festival of Sukkos,
therefore the primary aspect of "mother" is in Sukkos.
And it is explained in the discourses,
that [the fact] that the future redemption will be in Nisan,
even though Nisan is the level of "daughter"
(lower than "sister" and "mother"),
is [because],
the superiority of "sister" and "mother" is connected with the existence of the working person
(for through his service he becomes a brother to the Holy One, blessed be He,
and beyond this, he, as it were, bestows influence upon the Holy One, blessed be He).
Therefore,
through the service of "sister" and "mother," one reaches
(and becomes a brother and a mother)
only the level of light that pertains to the chain of descent
(the existence of the person).
And the superiority of "daughter"
(who has nothing of her own and is only a receiver from Above)
is in the matter of self-nullification.
And through this, one reaches the very Essence of Ein Sof.
And this is that in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed,
for in the future redemption there will be a revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof,
and this revelation is through self-nullification
[for this is that which is written of Moshiach,
"a poor man riding on a donkey,"
specifically "poor"],
the level of "daughter."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelations of the future depend specifically on our service in exile because the essence of self-nullification is primarily in the service during exile.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the reason why these revelations of the future depend specifically on our deeds and service during the time of exile,
is,
that the matter of self-nullification is primarily in the service during the time of exile.
And as explained elsewhere,
in the service during the time of the Holy Temple,
since there was then perception of G-dliness and they would "ascend on foot" and also see G-dliness,
the existence of the person who perceives and sees was also felt,
but in the time of exile,
and especially in the generation of the heels of Moshiach,
the service is in self-nullification,
not from the perspective of the person's existence, but only from the perspective of G-dliness.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the strength of these generations to withstand all trials comes from the service of "daughter" (self-nullification to G-d), which is above limitation and is hinted at in the fact that the level of "daughter" in exile is above the three festivals.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the power that exists in these generations to withstand all the trials that did not exist
(as much)
in previous generations,
including the trial of not being ashamed before those who mock,
which is a very great trial,
is,
that when a person withstands a trial by strengthening his own powers,
since his powers are measured and limited,
there are things that he is not capable of overcoming,
but not so in the generation of the heels of Moshiach,
where the service is in the aspect of "daughter,"
not from the perspective of the powers he has, but from the perspective of his self-nullification to G-d,
it is therefore understood,
that regarding G-dliness, there are no limitations.
And it can be said,
that this matter
(the superiority of the aspect of "daughter" during the time of exile)
is hinted at in what is explained in the discourses
(cited above)
that the three matters of "daughter," "sister," and "mother" correspond to the three pilgrimage festivals.
The order of these three matters, that "daughter" is lower than "sister" and "mother,"
is like they correspond to the three pilgrimage festivals,
the time of the Holy Temple.
But the aspect of "daughter" during the time of exile,
which is the self-nullification stemming from the essence of the soul,
is not included in these three matters
and is above them.
